messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: QBR blocker catalog + dependency map (action: updates by EOD)

Team —

As we finalize the QBR pack tomorrow, I need a concise blocker catalog mapped to owners and downstream dependencies. This is primarily for the product / eng slide deck and for the exec risk heatmap. Please update the shared spreadsheet (link below) with the following rows for any open work you own:

- Short blocker title (1 line)
- Severity: P0/P1/P2
- Root cause (one short sentence)
- Impacted launches/routes (list)
- Blocking dependency (team, JIRA id if available)
- ETA for mitigation / expected rollback plan

Key asks:
- Karthik: please add the list of mid-April release items that are currently failing end-to-end tests and call out whether the DB migration is required for the fix.
- Irene: confirm infra capacity + failover plan for the 99th percentile latency issue and whether the infra change can be staged before the QBR.
- Vivek: I may loop you in on any escalations tomorrow morning for prioritization.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0A1Qq-example-qbr-assets
Spreadsheet: qbr_blocker_catalog_v1.xlsx

Thanks — short bullet updates by EOD today so I can synthesize into one slide.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR blocker catalog + dependency map (action: updates by EOD)

Monica — updating the sheet now. Summary for the release group:

1) E2E test failures on "streaming-stream-splits" (P0)
   - Root cause: race condition in KV cache warmup when split shards are routed to new instances during a scale-up.
   - Impact: affects hosted API streaming for models with >8k context (customers: Acme Media internal staging).
   - Blocking dependency: INFRA-4521 (routing change), ETA: mitigation branch by 2027-04-10; hotfix possibility by toggling older routing policy (work-around) within 48h.

2) DB migration needed for model-metadata normalization (P1)
   - Root cause: inconsistent schema for model profiles created before 2026-09.
   - Impact: can cause 502s during model selection under load; affects Dedicated and Private customers for certain routing policies.
   - Blocking dependency: PROD-9876 (DB migration ticket). ETA: window scheduled 2027-04-16; risk of extended downtime if rollback not validated.

3) Canary tokenization mismatch (P2) — minor, will be in next sprint.

Notes: for (1) I will add a short rollback play to the spreadsheet (toggle routing flag) and mark a communication owner. If infra cannot support the temporary routing, we need to escalate to Vivek for capacity allotment.

Attachments: Added rows to qbr_blocker_catalog_v1.xlsx

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 14:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR blocker catalog + dependency map (action: updates by EOD)

On Sun, Apr 4, 2027 at 11:02 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Monica — updating the sheet now. Summary for the release group:
>
> 1) E2E test failures on "streaming-stream-splits" (P0)

Thanks Karthik — a couple infra notes to add into the sheet and the infra diagram (attached):

- Capacity: we have one spare node group in us-west-2 that can be used for short-term routing experiments; however, that group lacks NVLink connectivity which degrades throughput on large context models. If we route heavy-cxt traffic there expect a 12-18% latency increase at p95.
- Failover plan: INFRA-4521 requires a change in the router reconciliation window. We can short-circuit reconciliation (fast-path) for QBR window but it requires a canary with performance telemetry for at least 2 hours before full switch.
- Mitigation: recommend we enable the routing flag for 6 hours during a low-traffic window, run the telemetry check, then flip to full for peak. That gives us a redemption path within the QBR week without a full rollback.

I attached infra-failover-diagram.pdf and updated the spreadsheet with the capacity notes and timings.

- Irene
Irene Choi
VP, Infrastructure & Reliability, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR blocker catalog + dependency map (action: updates by EOD)

Thanks for the quick updates. Final synthesis for the exec deck:

- P0: streaming-stream-splits — mitigation path exists (routing toggle) but we need a signed risk acceptance for transient p95 degradation if we use the spare node group. Monica, please capture the trade-offs (latency delta vs. customer impact) in one slide and include the communication owner.
- P1: DB migration — this is our calendar risk for mid-April. If testing shows instability, we delay the migration and surface the decision during QBR with clear rollback criteria; should be marked as "calendar dependency" on the slide.
- P2: tokenization mismatch — low impact, no exec action required.

Next steps:
- Monica: consolidate Karthik/Irene rows into the single slide and share v1 with me by 9am PT tomorrow.
- Karthik: prepare the rollback toggle command and runbook (put in Drive).
- Irene: schedule 2-hour canary window and add perf telemetry sample to the shared Drive folder.

Also, I will join the customer-facing sync with Acme Media tomorrow at 11:30am PT to cover expectations and provide the honest trade-off note (cc Claire Huang). Monica, please add the Acme SOW doc to the shared folder so procurement has the latest.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
SVP, Product & GTM, Redwood Inference
